question: A 62-year-old woman is evaluated for fatigue 6 months after placement of a mechanical valve due to aortic stenosis. She does not drink alcohol or smoke cigarettes. A complete blood count reports hemoglobin of 9.5 g/L and a reticulocyte percentage of 5.8%. Platelet and leukocyte counts are within their normal ranges. The patient’s physician suspects traumatic hemolysis from the patient’s mechanical valve as the cause of her anemia. Which of the following peripheral blood smear findings would most support this diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Mechanical valve placement -> traumatic hemolysis -> anemia -> peripheral blood smear findings -> 80% CHAIN: Anemia -> increased reticulocyte percentage -> hemolysis -> mechanical valve -> 70% CHAIN: Hemoglobin 9.5 g/L -> anemia -> mechanical valve -> hemolysis -> peripheral blood smear findings -> 80%
analysis: The presence of RBC fragments and schistocytes on the peripheral blood smear is most indicative of traumatic hemolysis, which can occur in patients with mechanical heart valves.
